label: Remodeler / General contractor
project: Kitchen remodel - 1960s ranch, open to dining room
summary: Full gut kitchen with a wall removed, new cabinets, quartz tops and a relocated sink.
billing: Small deposit at signing (California caps it at 10% or $1,000, whichever is less), then progress payments tied to completed phases (demo/rough-in, drywall, cabinets and tops), final payment at punch list sign-off. CSLB: no payment ahead of work done or materials delivered.
ms: Done means demo is complete, the beam for the wall removal is in, and rough plumbing and electrical passed city inspection.
Done means insulation inspection passed, drywall is taped and textured, and tile floor is set and grouted.
Done means all cabinets are installed and level, quartz is templated, fabricated and installed, and the sink is set.
Finish, final inspection and punch list
Done means appliances and fixtures are working, final inspection passed, and every punch item on the walkthrough list is closed.
Punch items closed and signed off
waiting: Final selections: the backsplash tile and cabinet hardware so they can be ordered before the cabinet install date.
ask: Zellige adds 2 weeks lead time; full slab adds about $2,400.
answered: Keep the window over the sink or move the sink to the island?
Keep the sink at the window; island gets a prep zone only.
checkin: - Done: rough electrical and plumbing passed inspection Tuesday
- Done: header beam in, wall to dining room is open
- Next: insulation inspection Thursday, drywall starts Monday
- Next: cabinet delivery confirmed for the 18th
- Needs from you: backsplash pick by Friday
- Needs from you: sign change order #2 (two extra recessed lights)
talk: Rough inspection passed this morning. Drywall crew starts Monday. Can you pick the backsplash by Friday so it lands before cabinets?
Great news. We are torn between the zellige and the subway. Can we see both against the cabinet sample?
Yes. I will bring both samples Thursday at 4 and leave them on the counter for the weekend.
anxieties: Is the schedule slipping and when can we use the kitchen again?
Will there be more change orders and what will the final total be?
Are the inspections passing and is the work hidden in the walls done right?
notes: Highly variable scope. Portal must handle permits and inspections as gates, change orders with client signature and price impact, selections with deadlines tied to lead times, daily logs with photos, and deliveries (cabinets, appliances). Deposit caps vary by state.

label: Roofing contractor
project: Full tear-off and architectural shingle replacement - 28 squares
summary: Hail-damaged roof replaced through homeowner insurance, with new underlayment, flashing and ridge vent.
billing: Retail: deposit at signing for materials, balance at completion. Insurance jobs: homeowner pays deductible plus first ACV check to start, recoverable depreciation is released by the carrier after the roofer sends completion photos and final invoice.
ms: Done means the claim is approved, scope matches the adjuster's estimate, and deductible plus ACV check are received.
Done means the reroof permit is issued and shingles, underlayment and flashing are delivered to the driveway.
Done means old roof is removed, decking repaired, new underlayment, flashing, shingles and ridge vent are installed, and the yard is magnet-swept.
Ice and water shield at valleys
Done means the final inspection passed, completion docs went to the carrier, and the depreciation check is paid.
waiting: Endorsing the insurance check (often co-payable to the mortgage company) and choosing the shingle color.
ask: Same price; HOA approval may be required for darker colors.
answered: Replace the gutters at the same time?
No, keep existing gutters; reattach after install.
checkin: - Done: adjuster approved the supplement for drip edge and ridge vent
- Next: materials drop Wednesday, tear-off Thursday weather permitting
- Needs from you: endorse the ACV check and mortgage company sign-off
- Needs from you: move cars out of the driveway Thursday 7am
talk: Materials arrive Wednesday. Forecast is clear so tear-off is Thursday at 7. Please move cars out of the driveway.
Will do. Will someone check the attic for nails coming through?
Yes, the crew lead covers attic items with tarps and does a walkthrough with you at the end of day.
anxieties: What if it rains while the roof is open?
How much extra will rotted decking cost?
When will insurance release the rest of the money?
notes: Two very different flows: retail cash jobs (2-3 day install) and insurance claims (weeks to months of adjuster, supplement and depreciation steps). Portal should show weather-dependent dates, the insurance money trail (ACV, deductible, depreciation, supplements), photos and permit/inspection status.

label: HVAC installer
project: Heat pump and air handler replacement - 3 ton, with duct sealing
summary: Replace 20-year-old gas furnace and AC with a ducted heat pump, sized from a Manual J load calculation.
billing: Deposit of roughly 10-30% at signing to order equipment, balance due at completion; many tie final payment to passing the mechanical permit inspection. Rebates and tax credits paperwork follow.
ms: Done means the Manual J is complete, equipment model numbers are in writing, and the deposit is paid.
Done means the mechanical permit is issued and equipment is in the warehouse.
Done means old equipment is removed, new heat pump and air handler are set, line set charged, and system commissioned.
Done means the city inspection passed and rebate and tax credit forms are submitted.
waiting: Being home for the inspection window and signing the utility rebate form.
answered: Keep gas furnace as backup (dual fuel)?
No, all-electric heat pump with electric heat strips.
checkin: - Done: install complete, system running and charged
- Needs from you: someone home for inspector access
- Needs from you: sign rebate form
talk: Your system is running. Inspector is scheduled Tuesday between 8 and noon. Can someone be home?
I can work from home Tuesday. Is it normal that the outdoor unit is louder at startup?
Yes for the first minutes of defrost. We logged startup readings; I will check it on the inspection visit.
anxieties: Is it sized right and will it actually keep the house comfortable?
When do I get my rebate money?
How long will we be without heat or AC?
notes: Short install (1-2 days) but long tail: permit inspection, rebates, tax credit docs, warranty registration, maintenance plan. Portal should treat rebates as tracked items with their own status.

label: Solar installer
project: 8.4 kW rooftop solar with 13.5 kWh battery
summary: 21-panel rooftop system with battery backup, cash purchase, net metering interconnection.
billing: Cash deals: small deposit at signing (e.g. $1,000), most of the balance at installation, final 10% after building department approval. Loans disburse in stages (closing, approval, completion and PTO).
ms: Done means the site survey is done, the panel layout and production estimate are approved, and the deposit is paid.
Done means the building permit is issued and the utility interconnection application is submitted.
Done means panels, inverter and battery are installed and the system passes the installer's commissioning check.
Done means the city inspection passed and the utility granted permission to operate (PTO); system is turned on.
waiting: Signing the utility interconnection agreement and HOA approval where required.
answered: Essentials panel: fridge, internet, lights, garage door.
checkin: - Next: city inspection after install, then utility PTO (1-6 weeks)
- Needs from you: e-sign utility interconnection agreement
- Needs from you: clear the garage wall for the battery
talk: Install is set for Monday. Please clear about 4 feet of garage wall for the battery.
Done. Once it is installed can we start using it right away?
Not until the utility grants PTO, usually 1-6 weeks after inspection. We will post it here the day it arrives.
anxieties: When can I turn it on (PTO)?
Is the roof going to leak?
Will it produce what was promised and when do I get the tax credit paperwork?
notes: The longest wait is out of the installer's control: permit, utility interconnection and PTO. Portal must show third-party gates (city, utility, HOA, lender) clearly separate from installer work.

label: Pool builder
project: Gunite pool and spa - 15x32 with travertine deck
summary: Inground gunite pool with attached spa, tanning ledge, travertine decking and automation.
billing: Tiny deposit (California caps pool down payments at $200 or 2%), then payments tied to excavation, gunite, deck and plaster; final after plaster and final inspection. Nevada law caps each stage share.
ms: Done means the design is approved, permit issued, layout painted and the hole dug to plan.
Done means steel and plumbing pass inspection and the gunite shell is shot and curing.
Done means waterline tile and coping are set, equipment pad is plumbed and wired, and the deck is poured or laid.
Done means interior finish is applied, pool is filled and chemically started, and final inspection passed.
waiting: Finish selections (tile, coping, plaster color) and the safety barrier/fence required before final inspection.
ask: Pebble adds about $4,800 and lasts longer.
answered: Raised spillover spa, 18 inches above water line.
checkin: - Next: water the shell twice daily for 7 days
- Next: tile and coping start the 22nd
- Needs from you: waterline tile pick
talk: Gunite is shot. Please water the shell morning and evening for the next 7 days. Payment 2 is now due.
Got it. How long until we can swim?
About 4-6 weeks if tile and deck stay on schedule; plaster is the last step.
anxieties: Why has nothing happened for two weeks?
How long until we can swim?
Surprise costs like rock or extra dirt haul-off
notes: Long gaps between trades cause most anxiety. Many inspections (pre-gunite, pre-deck, barrier, final). Rock excavation and soil haul-off are classic change orders. Weather and cure times matter.

label: Custom home builder
project: New 3,200 sq ft custom home - Lot 14, Ridgeview
summary: Ground-up 4-bed custom home on an owner's lot, financed with a construction loan.
billing: Bank draw schedule: typically 5-7 draws tied to verified stages (foundation, framing, dry-in, rough-ins, drywall/trim, completion), each released after a lender inspection, with retainage held to the end.
ms: Done means the slab is poured and the foundation inspection passed.
Done means framing is complete, roof is on, windows are in and the house is weather-tight.
Done means plumbing, electrical and HVAC rough-ins passed and drywall is finished.
Done means finishes are installed, final inspections passed, CO issued and the walkthrough punch list is closed.
waiting: Selections on deadline (flooring, plumbing fixtures, lighting) and draw approvals from the lender.
ask: Needed before siding order; 3 week lead time.
answered: Upgrade to 10 ft ceilings on the main floor?
checkin: - Done: windows installed, house is dried in
- Needs from you: plumbing fixture selections by the 30th
- Needs from you: approve draw 2 with the bank
talk: House is dried in and framing passed. Draw 2 request went to the bank today. Fixture selections are due the 30th.
Exciting. Can we walk the framing this weekend to check outlet placement?
Yes, Saturday at 10. Bring your list; it is the cheapest time to move outlets.
anxieties: Are we on budget, and what do allowance overages add?
When is move-in, really?
Is the bank releasing draws and are subs getting paid (liens)?
notes: Longest timeline (8-18 months). Portal must handle selections with deadlines, allowances vs actuals, change orders, lender draws and inspections, lien waivers, and a big photo log.

label: ADU / garage conversion builder
project: Detached 600 sq ft ADU - 1 bed, 1 bath
summary: Detached backyard ADU with separate utilities, from plans through certificate of occupancy.
billing: California: down payment capped at $1,000 or 10%; progress payments tied to completed stages; CSLB issued a 2024 warning about ADU builders taking payments ahead of work. Design and permitting often billed separately.
ms: Done means plans are approved by the city and the building permit is issued.
Done means utility trenches are dug, lines run, and the foundation is poured and inspected.
Done means framing, rough-ins and insulation passed and drywall is up.
Done means finishes are in, final inspection passed and certificate of occupancy issued.
waiting: Responses to city plan-check questions and utility (electric meter) applications.
ask: Separate meter adds cost and utility wait but is better for renting.
checkin: - Needs from you: sign utility application
talk: City sent second-round corrections; we resubmitted today. Expect permit in 2-3 weeks.
Is that normal? We hoped to break ground this month.
Yes, two rounds is typical. We will schedule trenching the day the permit issues.
anxieties: How long will the city take?
Total cost including utility hookups and impact fees
Am I paying ahead of work?
notes: Permitting and utility hookups dominate the timeline; portal should show city plan-check rounds as visible steps.

label: Landscaping / Hardscape
project: Backyard paver patio, fire pit and planting
summary: 600 sq ft paver patio with seat wall, gas fire pit, drip irrigation and new planting beds.
billing: Design fee often credited toward the build; deposit at signing (ranges from 10% to 40-50%), a payment before work starts or after base compaction, then after pavers are laid, balance at final walkthrough.
ms: Done means the plan and material selections are approved and the deposit is paid.
Done means area is excavated, base gravel installed and compacted to spec.
Gas line stubbed for fire pit
Done means pavers, seat wall and fire pit are installed, cut and jointed with polymeric sand.
Done means planting and irrigation are in, timer programmed, and final walkthrough done.
waiting: Choosing plants and paver color, and HOA approval for visible changes.
ask: Tumbled adds about $1.50 per sq ft.
answered: Gas, with a stub from the existing meter.
checkin: - Needs from you: confirm plant list
talk: Base passed compaction. Pavers arrive Tuesday, install starts Wednesday.
Great. Can we see the plant list again?
Posted it here with photos of each plant; please confirm by Friday.
anxieties: Rain delays
Damage to lawn and sprinklers from equipment
Will plants survive / warranty
notes: Weather dependent; utility locates, HOA approval and material deliveries are key gates. Plant warranty and maintenance upsell after completion.

label: Interior designer
project: Living and dining room design - full furnish
summary: Full-service design for living and dining rooms: concept, furniture sourcing, procurement and install day.
billing: Design retainer at start (often 25-50% of estimated design fee), phase-based design fees, procurement paid up front by the client before orders (often cost plus 20-35% markup), install billed separately with balance before install day.
ms: Done means the concept board, layout and budget are approved.
Done means every item on the furnishing plan has an approved selection.
Done means all approved items are paid, ordered and tracked to the receiving warehouse.
Done means furniture is delivered, placed and styled, and punch items are logged.
waiting: Approving and paying procurement proposals so items can be ordered.
answered: No, replace with an 84 inch walnut table.
checkin: - Next: sofa ships week of the 12th
- Needs from you: approve rug proposal
talk: The rug proposal is ready. Approving today keeps install on the 3rd.
Approved. Is the sofa still on backorder?
Sofa ships the week of the 12th; we will update tracking here.
anxieties: Where is my furniture / backorders
Budget creep
Will it look like the renderings
notes: Procurement tracking (dozens of items with vendors, lead times, damage claims) is the core portal need; approvals per item.

label: Residential architect
summary: Design and permit drawings for a 900 sq ft second-story addition, plus construction administration.
billing: Fee as percent of construction cost or fixed fee, billed by AIA phase; a common illustrative split is 15% schematic design, 20% design development, 40% construction documents, 5% bidding, 20% construction administration (AIA does not set these).
ms: Done means the client approves a floor plan and massing concept.
Done means plans, elevations and key materials are fixed and engineer is engaged.
Done means the permit set is complete and the city issues the permit.
Done means a contractor is selected and site visits and RFIs are handled through completion.
waiting: Feedback on design options and decisions that unblock drawings (window style, roof form).
answered: Yes, primary bath with walk-in shower.
checkin: - Needs from you: confirm window style
talk: DD set is posted. The engineer needs the window style to size headers.
We like the black frame casements.
Noted. We will reflect casements in the CD set.
anxieties: How long until permit
Will it cost what we expect to build
Design review / neighbor objections
notes: Deliverable is drawings, not construction. Portal should show drawing sets, versions, plan-check rounds, RFIs; construction cost estimates sit with a separate contractor.

label: Custom cabinetry / furniture maker
project: Custom built-ins - family room wall and window seat
summary: Painted maple built-ins with bookshelves, media cabinet and window seat, designed, built and installed.
billing: Common: 50% when shop drawings are approved and order placed, 40% on delivery, 10% at substantial completion of install; larger jobs split 40/30/30.
ms: Done means the client signed shop drawings and finish samples.
Done means boxes, doors and faces are built and sprayed.
Done means pieces are delivered and checked for damage.
Done means built-ins are scribed, installed, touched up and accepted.
waiting: Signing shop drawings and approving the finish sample.
ask: Custom colors add a sample round.
talk: Boxes are done. Spraying this week. Please confirm the brass pulls.
Confirmed brass.
Thanks, delivery stays the 20th.
anxieties: Lead time
Will the finish match the sample
Fit against uneven walls
notes: Approval of shop drawings is the key gate; production is invisible to clients so progress photos matter.

label: Home inspector
project: Pre-purchase inspection - 2,100 sq ft single family
summary: Full buyer inspection with sewer scope and radon test inside a 10-day contingency.
billing: Paid in full at time of inspection or before the report is released; add-ons (sewer scope, radon) priced separately.
ms: Done means the date is booked and the inspection agreement is signed.
Done means the onsite inspection is complete and the fee paid.
Done means the report with photos is delivered within 24-48 hours.
Report sent to buyer and agent
Done means buyer questions are answered before the contingency deadline.
waiting: Payment and signed agreement before the report is released.
ask: Recommended for homes older than 30 years.
talk: Inspection done; report tomorrow evening.
Anything major?
Roof is near end of life; details in the report.
anxieties: Deal-breakers
Report timing vs contingency
Repair costs
notes: Single-day job; the portal value is report delivery and contingency deadline. Weak fit for multi-milestone portal.

label: Moving company
summary: Full pack, load, transport and unload with valuation coverage.
billing: Deposit to reserve, balance at delivery; interstate moves follow FMCSA rules (binding vs non-binding estimates; non-binding cannot exceed 110% at delivery).
ms: Done means the in-home or virtual survey is done and the estimate signed.
Done means all items are packed and labeled.
Done means truck is loaded and in transit with ETA.
Done means items are delivered, placed, balance paid.
waiting: Final inventory changes and access details (elevator reservation, parking).
talk: Truck departed; delivery window Thursday 8-12.
Can you call an hour ahead?
Yes, driver will call.
anxieties: Where is my stuff
Final price vs estimate
Damage claims
notes: Short projects; key is delivery window and inventory/claims.

label: Cleaning (post-construction / deep clean)
summary: Rough clean, final clean and touch-up clean before owner move-in.
billing: Priced per sq ft per phase (rough, final, touch-up); invoice per phase or on completion; GCs often net 30.
ms: Done means debris and heavy dust removed before finishes.
Done means all surfaces, fixtures and windows cleaned.
Done means post-punch dust cleaned before move-in.
waiting: Site access and confirmation that trades are finished.
talk: Rough clean is done; photos are posted. When do painters wrap so we can book the final clean?
Painters finish Friday. Owner walkthrough is Wednesday.
Then final clean Monday and touch-up Tuesday afternoon, ready for Wednesday.
anxieties: Dust remains
Timing vs move-in
Damage to finishes
notes: Depends on GC schedule; photo proof matters.

label: Home stager
person: Erin Walsh (listing agent) and seller Paul Grant
summary: Vacant home staged for listing photos with a 60-day rental term.
billing: Consultation fee (often credited), staging fee covering design, delivery and first 30-90 days rental, then monthly extensions; destage at sale or term end.
ms: Done means walkthrough and proposal accepted.
Done means furniture and decor installed before photos.
Done means term running; extension billed monthly.
Done means items removed after sale.
waiting: Listing date and access for install; notice of sale for destage.
talk: Staging is installed and photo-ready. Your 60-day term starts today.
Looks great. If we go under contract early, when do you pick up?
We destage within 3 business days of your notice, usually right before the final walkthrough.
anxieties: Ready for photos
Extension costs
Damage
notes: Client is often the agent; term and extension dates matter.
